ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening in accordance with OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Vietnam's domestic sanctions and politically exposed persons (PEP) blacklist maintained by the State Bank of Vietnam and the Ministry of Public Security. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is required for PEPs obtaining insurance, lending or digital financial services, spanning identity verification, source of wealth, source of funds, and continuous transaction monitoring under Law No. 14/2022/QH15 and SBV Circular No. 40/2019/TT-NHNN.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A company name must be written in Vietnamese, using letters of the Vietnamese alphabet, natural numbers, and symbols, and may include a short English equivalent provided the Vietnamese legal name remains the statutory name. All foreign-language legal names of shareholders and any transliterations must be romanized into the Vietnamese script for the enterprise registration docket; use of accented Vietnamese characters is compulsory for the statutory name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a rejection notice issued by the Department of Planning and Investment, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Director of the submitting provincial DPI within 30 days from the rejection date, in accordance with the Law on Complaints No. 02/2011/QH13. The appeal must identify the ground of refusal, attach the original DPI rejection notification, and propose an alternative name. A simultaneous application for a new name may be filed on the National Business Registration Portal to avoid delay. DPI must decide within 30 days of receiving a valid appeal; if the appeal is rejected, the applicant may further escalate to the provincial People's Committee or file a judicial review at the competent administrative court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible — a licensed business address service can provide a registered address for back-office and correspondence functions; however, for a P2P micro-lending platform requiring a statutory license from the State Bank of Vietnam, a physical office with verifiable presence and staff in the registered province is mandatory. The tax authority and SBV require actual management and record-keeping functions to be locatable in Vietnam.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High likelihood — approximately 65% annual probability of an unannounced or very short-notice on-site inspection by the State Bank of Vietnam, provincial DOI, and market surveillance authorities during the first year of licensed operations, with increased intensity for technology-based micro-lending models.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: General Department of Taxation of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam (Tong cuc Thue) under the Ministry of Finance; national tax e-filing portal: https://etaxvn.gdt.gov.vn; electronic declaration portal: https://thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn; foreign supplier information portal: https://fsr.gdt.gov.vn
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-invested LLC: (1) obtain an Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) from the provincial Department of Planning and Investment or the relevant industrial/export processing zone authority as applicable; (2) obtain an Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC); the enterprise code stated on the ERC is automatically the statutory tax identification number (MST) and serves simultaneously as the CIT, VAT, and payroll tax identification number; (3) activate electronic tax filing registration through eTaxVN at the provincial tax office using the issued TIN and digital certificate; (4) for a foreign digital supplier without a local legal entity, register directly on the General Department of Taxation's Foreign Supplier Portal and obtain a foreign supplier TIN, after which VAT and foreign contractor tax are declared and paid online. A separate physical VAT registration certificate is not required because the MST is the unified tax identity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Vietnam does not provide a U.S.-style check-the-box election; a VN LLC is treated as a non-pass-through, separately taxable corporate entity for CIT purposes. Domestic tax law does not recognize foreign entity classification elections or hybrid mismatch elections. The only available elective mechanisms are: (i) election between the VAT credit (deduction) method and the direct method on value-added/turnover for qualifying newly established or small enterprises, subject to General Department of Taxation approval; (ii) formal application for investment-promotion CIT incentive certificates rather than an elective entity classification; (iii) in the cross-border context, foreign suppliers may elect to either register directly under the Foreign Supplier Portal or have a Vietnamese counterparty withhold foreign contractor tax; and (iv) loss carry-forward utilization through annual CIT finalization, subject to the statutory five-year limitation. None of these mechanisms changes the default entity-level taxation of the LLC.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No VAT registration exemption or economic turnover threshold applies to a resident LLC; compulsory VAT registration begins from the first taxable supply. A statutory monetary exemption threshold of VND 100,000,000 in annual revenue applies only to small household businesses and individual taxpayers. Foreign digital suppliers providing e-commerce or digital services to Vietnamese customers are required to register and pay VAT through the Foreign Supplier Portal from the first supply with no turnover threshold, under Decree 85/2021/ND-CP and implementing tax circulars. For a P2P lending platform, credit extension and interest income are VAT-exempt financial services, while separately invoiced platform, underwriting, and collection facilitation fees are standard-rated VAT supplies at 10%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic invoicing is mandatory for all VAT taxpayers under Decree 123/2020/ND-CP and Circular 78/2021/TT-BTC. Invoices must be issued through a GDT-approved electronic invoicing system. Where pre-coded invoices are used, the invoice must carry a tax authority authentication code generated by the GDT national e-invoice system; where non-precoded e-invoices are used, invoice data must be transmitted electronically to the GDT within the legally prescribed period. Retail and point-of-sale service businesses, including fintech platforms, must use cash-register e-invoices with real-time data transmission to the tax authority. The LLC must integrate its lending and platform systems with Vietnam's e-invoice APIs or use a GDT-certified service provider to ensure timely clearance and digital stamping/authentication of all invoices. P2P loan interest is excluded from invoicing as a taxable supply, but platform fees and service charges require compliant e-invoicing with 10% VAT.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Vietnam qualify for the 0% VAT rate where the seller maintains an export contract, a customs-validated export declaration, transport documentation, and evidence that the goods left Vietnam, including sales to export processing enterprises. Services supplied to foreign organizations/individuals may qualify for 0% VAT if the services are performed for use outside Vietnam, the customer is a non-resident, and payment is received from abroad in foreign currency. For the fintech/P2P lending platform, algorithm-based underwriting or platform services supplied to a foreign customer may potentially be zero-rated if true offshore consumption is demonstrable; lending and credit-related activities generally remain VAT-exempt rather than zero-rated. Exporters with residual input VAT attributable to zero-rated exports of at least VND 300,000,000 may apply for a refund after the relevant month/quarter, provided all documentary substantiation is complete and no tax arrears exist.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration duly accepted by Vietnam Customs; for exported services, an executed export service contract and service performance/delivery certificate in lieu of customs declaration
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing export movement; for services, customer acceptance/consumption certificate proving offshore performance and use
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT credit advice confirming foreign-currency payment received from the non-resident customer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to documentary audit by the General Department of Taxation for five years from the statutory filing date, extending to ten years where omission, evasion, or fraud is indicated. If substantiation fails, the 0% rate is denied, input VAT refunds are clawed back with retrospective effect, and the taxpayer must pay the deficient output VAT, a 20% underpayment penalty, and late-payment interest at 0.03% per day. Administrative penalties for irregular invoices and false export declarations may reach three times the evaded tax amount. Criminal liability for VAT export fraud and tax evasion under Article 200 of the Penal Code includes fines up to VND 4.5 billion and imprisonment up to seven years for individuals, with higher penalties for organized schemes. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within the mandatory 180-day period also exposes the enterprise to foreign-exchange control penalties imposed by the State Bank of Vietnam.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Bank of Vietnam (Ngân hàng Nhà nước Việt Nam; SBV), acting as the central bank and the exclusive authority over the foreign exchange control regime of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam. Regulation and enforcement are exercised by the Foreign Exchange Control Department (Vụ Quản lý ngoại hối) and the Banking Supervision Agency, which jointly administer foreign currency licensing, registration of Direct Investment Capital Accounts, approval of foreign loans, determination of the mandatory surrender ratio, and sanctioning powers under the Foreign Exchange Ordinance No. 06/2005/PL-UBTVQH11 (as amended by Ordinance No. 10/2016/UBTVQH13) and its implementing instruments, notably Circular No. 15/2015/TT-NHNN (as amended by Circular No. 06/2019/TT-NHNN), Circular No. 05/2017/TT-NHNN, and Circular No. 08/2023/TT-NHNN.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Vietnamese Dong (VND) is conditionally convertible: current-account transactions are freely convertible at SBV-licensed credit institutions upon presentation of underlying transaction documents and declaration of the applicable payment/remittance purpose code prescribed by Circular No. 05/2017/TT-NHNN, whereas capital-account transactions require prior SBV registration or approval and are executed exclusively through the legally registered Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) of the foreign-invested LLC. Profit remittance is permissible but subject to four cumulative hurdles: (i) audited annual financial statements prepared under Vietnamese Accounting Standards showing net distributable after-tax profit; (ii) full settlement of all prior-year losses, corporate income tax, and other payable obligations; (iii) completion of annual enterprise information reporting and confirmed foreign-investor capital contribution records; and (iv) presentation of the bank certificate of capital contribution, DICA registration confirmation, and the board resolution approving dividend distribution. For a P2P micro-lending platform classified as High-Risk Special License, the bank will additionally scrutinize the credit-loss reserve, borrower receivables concentration, and the valid statutory license before executing any dividend or profit-stream remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The mandatory foreign-currency surrender ratio for export proceeds of goods and services is currently 0% as set by the State Bank of Vietnam's annual surrender decisions, meaning the foreign-invested LLC may retain all export service receipts in foreign currency or voluntarily convert them into VND. Nevertheless, the statutory repatriation mandate remains fully in force: all foreign-currency proceeds arising from exports of services, fintech fees, algorithmic underwriting service fees, or cross-border platform revenues must be brought back to Vietnam and credited to a licensed credit institution through the DICA within 180 days from the date of completion of the export service procedure as evidenced by the underlying transaction documentation. The treasury must map each inbound SWIFT credit to the corresponding invoice and service contract, record the balance-of-payment transaction code on the bank's FX application, and retain the full 180-day repatriation dossier at the relationship branch; failure to repatriate constitutes an exchange-control violation punishable under the Foreign Exchange Ordinance and Decree No. 88/2019/ND-CP (as amended by Decree No. 143/2021/ND-CP), including administrative monetary penalties and possible suspension of the enterprise's FX accounts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.special_licensing_note: The platform's target banking and FX structure is conditional upon possession of the statutory license referenced in the business scope metadata. P2P lending activity is not specifically licensed under Decree No. 96/2016/ND-CP, and in practice the platform must operate through a licensed credit institution or a licensed payment intermediary service provider under Decree No. 52/2024/ND-CP. The DICA and FX structuring set out in this blueprint assume the entity has obtained the required balance-sheet partnership arrangement with an SBV-licensed bank or credit institution and, where applicable, an SBV license for payment intermediation services, before treasury accounts are activated.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.reporting_and_data_residency_note: All cross-border capital flows into and out of the DICA must be reported by the onboarding bank to the SBV under the BOP reporting regime. The platform must maintain a resident compliance officer responsible for preparing and submitting the quarterly enterprise FX flow reports if so required by the bank agreement, and any direct cross-border lending by the platform without an SBV license is strictly prohibited. Payments involving the platform's beneficiaries outside Vietnam must not involve VND offshore settlement; VND is not freely deliverable outside Vietnam, and all VND-denominated flows with non-residents must be executed through the onshore DICA of a licensed bank.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Information Confirmation (xác nhận thông tin đăng ký doanh nghiệp)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Business Registration Portal (Ministry of Planning and Investment integrated system) with confirmation at the Provincial Department of Planning and Investment holding the enterprise file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Every calendar year from 1 January through 30 July; a newly registered enterprise must complete first confirmation within 30 days of Enterprise Registration Certificate issuance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of VND 5,000,000 – 10,000,000 under Decree 122/2021/ND-CP; repeated non-confirmation triggers forced re-registration and, in persistent cases, administrative revocation of the Enterprise Registration Certificate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business License Duty (lệ phí môn bài) – corporate franchise levy / license fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Tax Department of the head office (declared and paid through the Electronic Tax Portal of the General Department of Taxation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 30 January; for enterprises newly licensed during the year, payment is due within 30 days of license issuance, with reduced first-year rates applying when registration occurs after specific cutoff dates
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 0.03% per day plus administrative tax fines up to VND 30,000,000 under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP; prolonged default enables tax-authority debt enforcement against corporate bank accounts and assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual CIT Finalization Return (tờ khai quyết toán thuế TNDN)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Tax Department of the foreign-invested LLC head office (General Department of Taxation electronic filing system)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year taxpayer, no later than 31 March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Escalating late-filing fines under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP from VND 2,000,000 up to VND 40,000,000 depending on the number of delinquent days, plus late-payment interest of 0.03% per day; sustained failure triggers enforced tax assessment, invoice suspension, asset seizure, and grounds for license revocation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Audited Financial Statements (báo cáo tài chính đã kiểm toán) submission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Department of Planning and Investment (foreign-invested enterprise licensing authority), Provincial Tax Department, and General Statistics Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after fiscal year-end for the standard financial statement filing (calendar-year taxpayer: by 31 March); audited opinions accompany the CIT finalization and the DPI annual compliance file, with the audited copy accepted on the DPI file within 30 days of the audit report signature date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to VND 20,000,000 for failure to file statutory accounting reports; three consecutive years of non-filing, together with tax-default evidence, may lead the provincial authority to suspend the Enterprise Registration Certificate and order dissolution procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Semi-Annual / Annual Fintech Sandbox and AML Compliance Report (P2P lending operations, portfolio quality, suspicious transaction reporting)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) – Payment Oversight Department and Banking Supervision Agency, through the local SBV provincial branch
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Semi-annual operational report within 30 days after 30 June; cumulative annual report by 31 January of the following year; the SBV sandbox permit may impose stricter individual filing dates
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: SBV administrative sanctions for regulated fintech and payment intermediaries, including fines for non-provision of prudential reports and AML returns; continued non-compliance beyond 60 days may suspend the P2P lending sandbox license and require orderly wind-down of outstanding borrower principals.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory annual independent audit for all foreign-invested enterprises regardless of turnover or asset thresholds; compulsory as a condition of the SBV fintech/P2P lending or payment-intermediary license; no micro-entity exemption applies. Audit must be performed by a Vietnamese-licensed independent auditing firm.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Vietnamese Accounting Standards (VAS) per Circular 200/2014/TT-BTC for statutory standalone financial statements; IFRS may be elected for supplementary consolidated or group-level reporting; foreign-invested entities must maintain accounting records in Vietnamese Dong.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Anti-Money Laundering Law 2022 (Decree 19/2023/ND-CP), the licensed P2P micro-lending platform must identify and verify every beneficial owner (individuals holding at least 25% of charter capital or exercising ultimate control) at onboarding, at each ownership transfer, and on a rolling annual basis. Member-register updates must be made within 10 days of any contribution or transfer transaction; a refreshed beneficial-ownership schedule must accompany the annual AML report and SBV sandbox return.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (multi-member LLC statutory register containing capital contribution percentages, payment status, and full transfer history)
Register of Directors and Members' Council appointments (resolutions underlying management appointments, resignations, and delegated authorities)
Minute Book (annual general meeting minutes, written resolutions, and Members' Council decisions kept permanently at the registered office)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 – USD 800 per year (serviced registered address in Ho Chi Minh City or Hanoi, corporate secretarial liaison for DPI notifications, tax correspondence handling, and statutory register maintenance)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,500 – USD 9,000 per year (VAS annual audit by a licensed local independent audit firm, including audited financial statements delivery and CIT finalization support)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% (standard corporate income tax for all resident enterprises, including foreign-invested limited liability companies)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No automatic tax holiday for fintech P2P lending platforms. General incentives that could apply upon satisfying statutory conditions for an eligible new investment project include: (1) 10% CIT for 15 years plus 4-year exemption and 50% reduction for 9 years for projects located in severely disadvantaged areas, high-tech zones, or engaged in encouraged high-tech/software sectors; (2) reduced rates of 15% CIT for SMEs with annual taxable revenue not exceeding VND 3 billion and 17% for SMEs with revenue from VND 3 billion to VND 50 billion (subject to employee and shareholding conditions); (3) 50% reduction for the first 2 years for certain newly established enterprises in industrial parks. A P2P micro-lending platform merely providing algorithmic underwriting and loan-broking services will normally bear the standard 20% rate; any claimed incentive must be evidenced by an investment certificate or tax incentive code issued by the competent tax authority.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 02/TNDN (Annual Corporate Income Tax Finalization Return) filed via the official e-Tax electronic filing portal of the General Department of Taxation (thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn / etax.vn) using the HTKK application and declared in XML 4.0 format under Circular 80/2021/TT-BTC and Decree 126/2020/ND-CP.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than the 90th day after the end of the fiscal year. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the deadline is 31 March of the following year. The annual finalization is also the compulsory deadline for the full settlement of prior quarterly provisional CIT payments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The 10-digit Vietnamese Enterprise Tax Identification Number assigned to the LLC by the provincial tax department upon incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign shareholders must accept the TIN of the Vietnamese legal entity; no separate Vietnamese TIN is needed by the foreign shareholder for CIT finalization unless it is subject to a withholding obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total net revenue from the lending platform: origination fees, commission from licensed consumer-finance partners, loan-servicing fees, late-payment charges, and any accrued interest if the company operates as balance-sheet lender.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Revenue must follow Circular 200/2014/TT-BTC (Vietnamese Accounting Standards). If the platform acts solely as an intermediary for a licensed credit institution, only the net agency commission is included in revenue; any mischaracterization triggers a reckless-declaration penalty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box C-01 (Chi phí được trừ / Deductible expenses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable expenses actually incurred, ordinary and necessary for the business, supported by lawful invoices/vouchers, including employee costs, cloud-hosting, software licensing, legal fees, amortization of software, and non-life insurance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to foreign vendors (e.g., cloud services, software-as-a-service, or royalty-bearing technology) are deductible only when the foreign contractor tax (FCT) has been withheld and remitted; where a cross-border contract is silent on tax, the grossed-up amount is used and only that amount is deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box D-01 (Thu nhập chịu thuế / Taxable income before loss offset)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue less deductible expenses plus all other taxable income, after the mandatory accounting-to-tax reconciliation of permanent and temporary differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The taxpayer must add back non-deductible provisions, non-deductible interest in excess of the 30%-EBITDA thin-cap cap, penalties, and expenses without valid invoices; the foreign shareholder cannot deduct group-management service charges unless arm's-length contracts and TP documentation exist.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses previously assessed and approved, carried forward and offset against current-year taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A loss may be carried forward for exactly 5 consecutive years from the year in which the loss arose; carry-back is prohibited. Carried losses survive a change in shareholder composition but not a business transfer or reorganization involving cessation of the business line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box F-01 (Thu nhập tính thuế / Assessable income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after the deduction of the eligible loss carry-forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The entry cannot be negative; if the year is again loss-making, Box E-01 records the new loss and Box F-01 is zero, with the loss re-commencing its 5-year cycle.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The applicable CIT rate, normally 20%; incentive rates of 10%, 15%, or 17% are entered only when supported by an unexpired tax incentive code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign shareholders must not assume any treaty-based rate applies at the entity level; CIT is a national tax levied on the Vietnamese entity, and the treaty does not reduce the entity rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box H-01 (Thuế TNDN phải nộp / CIT payable)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessable income in Box F-01 multiplied by the rate in Box G-01.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the final annual CIT liability of the Vietnamese LLC. Subsequent dividend distribution to the foreign corporate shareholder no longer triggers any corporate withholding tax in Vietnam.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box I-01 (Thuế tạm nộp / Quarterly provisional payments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sum of the quarterly CIT provisional payments made during the year using Form 01/TNDN (including the fourth-quarter settlement paid with the finalization).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provisional payments must reach at least 80% of the final annual CIT payable; an underpayment of the 80% threshold attracts a fine equal to 20% of the shortfall plus late-payment interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box J-01 (Còn phải nộp / Additional tax or refund)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The difference between the final CIT payable in Box H-01 and the provisional payments in Box I-01; a positive balance is payable by the statutory deadline, a negative balance becomes a refund request.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A tax refund to the collapsing company is paid within 6 months of the closing of the tax file; the foreign shareholder cannot offset such refunds against unrelated Vietnamese tax obligations except under strict offset rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an administrative fine tiered at VND 1.25 million, VND 2.5 million, VND 5 million, VND 8 million, and up to VND 15-50 million for delays exceeding 60 days (Decree 125/2020/ND-CP); in all cases, late-payment interest accrues at 0.03% per day (approximately 10.95% per annum) from the statutory due date. Failure to pay within 90 days after the finalization deadline additionally exposes the company to enforced tax collection, bank-account freezes, and involuntary asset auction; underpaid amounts discovered during tax inspection attract a 20% penalty on the under-declared tax rather than the smaller 15% misdemeanor rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 01/TNDN (Quarterly Corporate Income Tax Provisional Declaration) filed via the e-Tax portal / HTKK software companion application.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly (for the first three fiscal quarters of the tax year; the fourth quarter is settled only in the annual finalization).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than the 30th day after the end of the respective quarter: 30 April for Q1, 31 July for Q2, and 31 October for Q3. For a fiscal year that does not align with the calendar year, the same 30-day rule applies to each quarter of that fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must match the code printed on the investment registration certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 2 – Cumulative estimated taxable income for the year-to-date
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prudent estimate of taxable income determined on a quarter-to-date basis, reflecting known permanent differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The estimate must not be artificially minimized; estimated income must be sufficient to trigger provisional payments meeting the 80% rule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 3 – Estimated CIT payable for the year-to-date
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Estimated taxable income multiplied by the statutory or incentive CIT rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Incentive rates may be used only where the incentive code is already valid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 4 – Less CIT paid in prior quarters
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sum of provisional amounts already remitted in earlier quarters.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No foreign currency conversion issues arise because the Vietnamese entity always declares and pays in VND.
The company must transfer the amount to the state budget using the allocated tax-account code before the quarterly deadline.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the quarterly provisional form is subject to fines from VND 5 million to VND 50 million depending on the number of days delayed; failure to remit the provisional tax due results in late-payment interest at 0.03% per day. The most serious consequence is the so-called '80% rule': if the sum of provisional payments is less than 80% of the final annual CIT liability, the taxpayer must pay a penalty equal to 20% of the shortfall plus the 0.03%-per-day interest from the applicable quarterly due date.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Domestic corporate dividend withholding tax: 0% (Vietnam imposes no withholding tax on dividends distributed by an LLC to a foreign corporate shareholder; distributions are made from the after-tax profit of the Vietnamese entity and are not re-taxed at the corporate level). Individual foreign shareholders are subject to a final personal income tax (PIT) withholding of 5% on dividend income. Under the Vietnamese double-taxation treaties, the common treaty allocation rates are 5-10% for dividends, but because the domestic law rate on corporate dividends is already 0%, no treaty claim is needed by a corporate shareholder; the 0% domestic outcome is always the maximum benefit.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For corporate shareholders, no TRC (Tax Residency Certificate) is required for an ordinary dividend distribution because the domestic law imposes a 0% withholding rate. Where treaty relief is nevertheless relevant (e.g., for an individual shareholder receiving dividends, or for interest/royalty payments under the Foreign Contractor Tax regime), the protocol is as follows: (1) The foreign recipient obtains an original Tax Residency Certificate from the competent tax authority of its country of residence; (2) the recipient submits the TRC, a Vietnamese-language summary declaration of residence and beneficial ownership, and, where applicable, a certificate that the beneficial owner holds a minimum shareholding (typically 25% or 35% depending on the treaty) to the Vietnamese company before the payment date; (3) the Vietnamese withholding agent files the prescribed withholding return and supporting attachments with the local tax authority before or at the time the reduced-rate payment is made; (4) the tax authority may respond within 5 working days; if silent, the reduced rate is applied at source; (5) if the TRC is not lodged by the payment date, the statutory rate must be withheld and the foreign recipient may file a subsequent claim for refund within the statute of limitations. The entire administrative procedure is governed by Circular 80/2021/TT-BTC on tax administration and the specific DTA article on dividends, interest, and royalties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: domestic Foreign Contractor Tax (FCT) withholding on interest paid to a foreign lender is 5% of gross interest (no VAT), because credit extension is exempt from VAT. Most Vietnamese DTAs set the interest withholding cap at 10%, but since the treaty may not worsen the domestic outcome, the effective rate is 5%. Royalty: domestic FCT on royalties for technology, software, trademark, and similar IP is an aggregate 15% of gross (10% deemed CIT plus 5% deemed VAT). Under most applicable DTAs, the CIT component is capped at 10% (and at 5% for royalties for the use of industrial, commercial, or scientific equipment in selected treaties), while the 5% VAT component remains irreducible in all cases; thus the effective aggregate is typically 15% (or 10% in the equipment-royalty scenario). The Vietnamese payor is the withholding agent and must file the FCT return on the date of payment; if the FCT is contractually borne by the Vietnamese company, the grossed-up amount (including the tax gross-up) must be declared and withheld on the grossed-up base.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: VND-denominated thresholds under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP. Local File (and related-party transaction forms) must be prepared if the taxpayer has any related-party transaction and meets at least one of the following: (1) total revenue from selling goods or providing services to related parties in the tax year exceeds VND 50 billion; (2) total value of related-party transactions (including loans, borrowings, purchase of assets, services, and interest paid) exceeds VND 30 billion; or (3) total interest expense and related loan costs paid during the tax year (including to unrelated parties) exceeds VND 20 billion. The Master File is mandatory when the ultimate parent (whether foreign or Vietnamese) of the group achieves consolidated revenue of VND 18,000 billion (approximately USD 750 million) or more. Country-by-Country Report is required when the Vietnamese ultimate parent entity has consolidated revenue of VND 18,000 billion or more and also for certain foreign-controlled groups meeting the same consolidated-revenue test. The related-party loan-interest deduction is further capped at 30% of the taxpayer's EBITDA (interest ratio cap); the disallowed excess interest may be carried forward to later years within the 5-year window.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vietnam does not operate a Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime, but the transfer-pricing law (Decree 132/2020/ND-CP) incorporates rigorous substance-over-form and anti-abuse doctrines: (1) the tax authority may disregard, recharacterize, or allocate income from a related-party transaction if the arrangement lacks commercial rationality or economic substance, or if one party the enterprise is related to is neither functionally nor risk-bearing capable of performing the purported functions; (2) BEPS Action 6 minimum-standard is applied to deny treaty benefits where a foreign investor is a mere conduit interposed mainly to obtain a Vietnamese DTA advantage; (3) the Vietnamese entity is expected to perform the core value-creating functions in-country – for a P2P/lending platform this means actual underwriting staff, credit-risk managers, data scientists, decision-makers, board meetings, servers/IT systems, and audited financials in Vietnam. A 'shell' LLC holding only legal title, with no employees or decision-making, will have its related-party transactions recharacterized and its attributable income increased; the tax authority may further assert a permanent establishment of the foreign parent in Vietnam.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Criminal False Declaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-declaration of platform origination fees or loan interest, systematic use of fabricated or third-party invoices to inflate deductible costs, non-filing of CIT returns after repeated reminders, or arranging artificial loss transfers to avoid the 20% statutory tax on the lending and service revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administratively, the under-declared amount is subjected to a fine equal to 20% of the underpaid tax plus late-payment interest at 0.03% per day (approximately 10.95% per annum). Criminally, the Penal Code (No. 100/2015/QH13, as amended by Law 12/2017/QH14) Article 200 applies: tax evasion from VND 100 million to under VND 300 million carries a fine of VND 100-500 million or non-custodial reform up to 3 years; evasion of VND 300 million or more, or with aggravating factors such as abuse of position, carries imprisonment of up to 5 years. A legal entity convicted of tax evasion is subject to a fine of up to VND 5 billion, suspension of activity for up to 36 months, and prohibition from doing certain lines of business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative (chairman, general director, CEO) and the chief accountant who sign or directly order the false return are individually criminally liable and may be imprisoned for 1-5 years. The tax authority can additionally impose a temporary exit ban (suspension of exit from Vietnam) on the responsible individual under Article 217 of the Law on Tax Administration, freeze personal bank accounts, seize and auction personal assets, and, in cross-border cases, transmit the dossier through mutual legal assistance and INTERPOL.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a peer-to-peer or balance-sheet micro-lending platform with the company's own capital or simultaneously matching retail lenders, without holding a credit-institution license from the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV), and failing to apply AML/KYC controls on retail borrowers and lenders – for example, accepting large structured cash deposits, serving sanctioned persons, or facilitating the movement of criminal proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administratively, SBV may impose fines up to VND 300-500 million and order the immediate cessation of the unlicensed lending operation, revocation of any incidental payment-intermediary license, and confiscation of gains. Criminally, Penal Code Article 180 (illegal operation of banking or other financial activities) applies: a natural person faces a fine of VND 100 million to VND 1 billion, imprisonment for up to 5 years, and a prohibition from business activity for up to 5 years; a legal entity faces fines up to VND 2 billion, suspension of operations, and compulsory deregistration. A fake or undercapitalized lending scheme directed at retail borrowers may also be prosecuted as fraud under Penal Code Article 174, carrying up to 12 years' imprisonment for an individual and corresponding corporate fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The directors and officers who designed or managed the illegal credit or lending scheme are criminally prosecuted personally; they face imprisonment, personal fines, asset seizures, and temporary exit bans. Under the Law on Prevention and Combating of Money Laundering (Law 14/2022/QH15), directors are also personally accountable for the implementation of AML policies; failure to report suspicious P2P transactions can lead to independent AML fines and criminal money-laundering charges under Penal Code Article 324, which carry imprisonment of up to 10 years for the natural-person manager.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Treaty-Abuse Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the Vietnamese LLC as a pure conduit with zero onshore substance: no employees, no physical office space, no board meetings in Vietnam, no risk-management staff, and all algorithmic underwriting, credit decisions, and profit-influential functions conducted offshore; or inserting the Vietnamese entity solely to enjoy a 0% dividend withholding result or another DTA advantage while the offshore parent continues to perform the entire business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The transfer-pricing authority will disregard the shell entity and will re-attribute income to the offshore principal; the Vietnamese LLC is then treated as a permanent establishment of the foreign company, subjecting the foreign principal to a 20% CIT on the Vietnam-attributable income plus a 20% understatement penalty and 0.03%-per-day interest. Payments labeled as interest or service fees from the shell to the offshore parent may be recharacterized as disguised dividends, losing any DTA benefit and incurring the same deficiencies. If the shell has obtained unjustified tax refunds, the refund can be clawed back with penalties, and the company risks being dissolved for operating outside the registered business purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly channel profits through an economically hollow Vietnamese entity are jointly and severally liable for the additional tax, interest, and penalties if the company becomes insolvent; they may be personally barred from the territory of Vietnam (exit ban) and from acting as managers of any Vietnamese enterprise for up to 3 years. In aggravated cases involving fictitious contracts, the responsible director incurs criminal liability for tax evasion; involvement in laundering the diverted funds triggers money-laundering prosecution with imprisonment of up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Foreign Contractor Tax (FCT) Non-Withholding or Disguised Remittance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying offshore technology providers, cloud platforms, software licensors, or group interest and deducting the full gross amount without withholding the required 5% (interest), 15% (royalty), or other applicable FCT rate; alternatively, characterizing an equity dividend as an artificially high 'interest payment' or 'management fee' to obtain the 5% interest withholding instead of a taxable profit extraction and simultaneously eroding the Vietnamese tax base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Vietnamese LLC, as the withholding agent, is liable for the un-withheld FCT on the full gross payment, plus late-payment interest at 0.03% per day, and an administrative fine equal to 20% of the under-withheld amount (or up to 1-3 times the omitted amount in cases of intentional failure). The offshore vendor is considered to have a permanent establishment in Vietnam if the contractual activity is performed in Vietnam, in which case the vendor is assessed on net profit rather than gross, with the increased tax being assessed to the Vietnamese payor on a joint-and-several basis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The CFO, chief accountant, and legal representative who authorized the foreign payments are individually obliged to ensure the FCT was withheld; if the company cannot satisfy the liability, the responsible directors' personal assets may be pursued, and the authority will issue a temporary exit suspension against them. A repeated pattern of non-withholding with a cumulative unremitted FCT exceeding VND 100 million is treated as criminal tax evasion, and the directors face imprisonment as well as civil restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer-Pricing Documentation Failure and Related-Party Interest Cap
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare the Local File, Master File, and the statutory transfer-pricing notification (Form 01 and related declarations) despite crossing any of the VND 50 billion revenue, VND 30 billion transaction, or VND 20 billion interest thresholds; paying offshore shareholder loans and deducting net interest exceeding 30% of EBITDA; or incorrectly benchmarking the arm's-length commission to the offshore software owner when the P2P underwriting algorithm is held by a related party.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Upon non-submission of TP documentation, the tax authority is entitled to determine the Vietnamese entity's income by reference to an adverse benchmark of comparable transactions and may apply a penalty equal to 20% of the additionally assessed CIT, plus 0.03%-per-day late interest. Administrative fines apply for failure to submit documents (categorized under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP at VND 40-70 million per occurrence). Interest expenses exceeding the 30% EBITDA cap are disallowed from deduction; the disallowed portion is not permanently lost but may be carried forward to the next tax year and across a maximum of the next 5 years, with a correspondingly heavier administrative burden to prove the carry-forward.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director and CFO are personally responsible for the completeness and truthfulness of the TP documentation attached to the annual CIT return. If the absence of documentation is coupled with an underpaid CIT in excess of VND 100 million, they are exposed to criminal tax evasion charges and imprisonment up to 5 years. Even without criminal referral, the tax authority will issue an exit ban and asset-freeze order against the responsible individual to secure the recovery of the assessed tax, penalties, and interest.
